Who the round's mail to a row's referent goes to

mail_referent.Rd

The row's owner: who the creation log names as having made the row, until an approved change by another referent hands it over, which the log holds as a write of owned_by by the channel's account. The round settles it from the log and passes it on as owner. It is the only one whose approval of a change counts, IT aside; the scope gate judges whoever wrote what the round carries out, which is the owner only when nobody else changed the row. Every message the round sends to whoever asked goes there: the outcome, whatever it is, and the key of an account just made.

Usage

mail_referent(row)

Arguments

row

One register row as a list, with this round's outcome and the owner the round settled.

Value

One address, possibly empty.

Details

Not requested_by. On the form @USERNAME fills it in and the two agree; the Data Import Tool writes it as the CSV has it (measured on 2026-09-02 and again on 2026-10-16), and the round does not write it back. Sent to that field, an import that left it empty lost the key and the outcome, and one naming another address sent both there, to the person themselves if the file said so, against the rule that the key stays with the referent.

And there is no fallback to it. Once a row can change hands, a fallback would write to a former owner, the one person who should no longer hear about the row. An empty owner means the round could not settle it, and the outcome then goes to IT alone and says so (see mail_round()). That happens on a sweep of the tenant that failed, which asks no log; on a creation log or an owners' log that could not be read; on a round with no row to judge, which asks neither; on a creation log that does not name the row; and on an owner the log cannot say, log_owner(), as when a write of owned_by with no author stands above the channel's. No key reaches anybody then: a row whose owner the log does not name stops at the gate on TRASPORTO_AUTORE_NON_LEGGIBILE, and nobody is made for it.
